increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them test gaps rather than defects. What shipped: a collector-side lane join in store.getAgents behind GET /api/sessions/:id/agents, giving every span of a session a lane key of 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed' by resolving agent_id first and the parent-span chain second; a timeline module in argus-ui drawing one bar per lane over one shared window; and the six technical views (overview, todos, traces, events, metrics, raw) moved into a strip below the timeline, closed by default. npm --prefix tools/argus test 176 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 39 cases exit 0. Both correction rounds were spent because the visible behaviour was computed by a tested pure helper but never pinned in the rendered markup or the booted page; the round-2 fake-DOM harness in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs now boots public/app.js in-process, so later UI increments have a way to pin what the human sees.

increments.title: Activity and context growth drawn on each lane
increments.goal: Draw each lane's activity over time and, behind it, that agent's context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows its activity over time - tool calls and API requests - placed at the times they occurred, on the lane of the agent instance the activity belongs to.

Activity is assigned to lanes with the lane vocabulary the session's agents endpoint already serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed'), not a second attribution scheme; the records drawn here carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated.
Activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane rather than being dropped or folded into the main lane.
Each lane carries, as a curve or area behind that activity, the context size over time for that agent.

The curve is drawn from a size the telemetry actually records - the reported untruncated request-body length survives even when the body itself was truncated - and the view names which measure it is showing.
Growth in context size is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.
What proves this increment is the drawn result in the page: a change that stops the activity marks or the curve reaching the rendered timeline is caught, not only a computation checked in isolation.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: store.getAgents now joins claude_code.tool and claude_code.llm_request spans into a per-lane activity list and api_request_body records into a per-lane context series, both on the existing 'main' / 'agent:<agent_id>' / 'unattributed' lane keys; the content records carry no agent_id, so their lane is resolved through their spanId and a record whose span is unknown lands on unattributed, never on main; a requestBodyLength helper prefers the reported body_length over the delivered body, so a truncated or body_ref-only record still reports its true size; timeline.js draws an SVG area per lane scaled to one session-wide peak with activity ticks over it and a legend naming the measure; and app.test.mjs boots the real page and pins that marks and a non-empty polygon reach the rendered timeline. npm --prefix tools/argus test 186 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 54 cases exit 0. The fake-DOM harness plus the provability criterion cost this increment zero correction rounds, against two for the increment before it.

increments.title: Scrubbing the timeline, and a live mode that follows the head
increments.goal: Give the timeline a chosen time that can be moved to any point of the recorded session, plus a live mode that follows the newest data as it arrives.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session, and the chosen time is visible on the timeline.
The chosen time is drawn against the same shared window the lanes are already drawn against, so its position lines up with the activity marks and the context curve at that instant.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives, and keeps following as later data extends the session's window.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode.
A control returns to live mode.
The chosen time is one shared value the session view works from, so a later per-lane detail can be answered for exactly that moment.

What proves this increment is the behaviour of the page: a change that stops scrubbing moving the chosen time, or stops the live control returning to the head, is caught, not only a helper that maps a position to a time.
increments.note: Re-cut after lane-activity. Two criteria sharpened, none added or removed in substance. Lane-activity drew the marks and the curve over one shared window with a session-wide scale, so the chosen time now has something concrete to line up with and the criterion says so; and it showed the /agents payload is refetched as ingest coalesces, which is what live mode has to keep following as the window's end moves. The provability criterion stands: it is what made lane-activity pass on the first round after timeline-landing spent two rounds on unpinned page wiring.

increments.title: The selected agent's context and tool use as of the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, that agent's or the main session's context at that moment as a structured, expandable message list, together with the tools that agent has used up to that moment.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent's - or the main session's - context as of that moment.

The lane selected is one of the lanes the timeline already draws, and the records shown are chosen by that lane and the chosen time using the lane vocabulary already in place, not a second attribution scheme.
The context shown is the body of the nearest API request at or before the chosen time.
It is rendered as a structured message list distinguishing system prompt, user, assistant, tool call and tool result blocks.
Each block is collapsed to one line carrying its size.
Each block expands to the exact full text the record carries, and a body the CLI truncated is marked as truncated instead of being presented as the whole context.
A record that reports a body length but carries no body text at all is shown as its reported size with the text stated to be absent, rather than as an empty context.
The same selection also shows the tools that agent has used up to that moment, each entry carrying the tool name and that call's parameters.
The tool listing is bounded by the same chosen time and the same lane as the context, so the two halves of the panel never disagree about who did what when.
Both listings are per agent and per time, so 'which tools, and what for' is answerable for any agent at any point of the session.

What proves this increment is the rendered panel: a change that stops a selection reaching the panel, or stops an expanded block showing the full text, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Re-cut after lane-activity. Kept whole and kept last; two criteria added. The first is a fact lane-activity uncovered: content records can arrive carrying only a reported body_length with no body and no body_ref, which is why the collector needed a length-preferring helper at all, so the panel has to have an answer for a block whose exact text does not exist rather than rendering nothing. The second pins that the tool listing and the context obey the same lane and the same time bound - cheap now, because lane-activity already serves each lane's tool and API activity with times and names on the /agents payload, so this increment adds the call parameters and the time bound rather than a third attribution scheme. That same reason confirms keeping the merged tools-at-time inside it.

increments.title: The selected agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, the tools that agent has used up to that moment together with the parameters of each call.
increments.note: Merged into context-at-time, which now carries all of its criteria. content-pipeline showed tool parameters arrive as the same content records as request bodies, retrieved through the same query with the same time bound and the same per-agent join; lane-activity then put each lane's tool calls, with names and times, on the /agents payload the panel already loads. Building this separately would repeat context-at-time's selection and attribution work for one extra list in the same panel.

return.summary: Closed lane-activity as done (review accepted, no findings, no correction rounds) and re-cut the two open increments against what it showed. Nothing was split, merged, dropped or reordered; the run confirmed the cut again. Three facts changed criteria. First, lane-activity drew every lane's marks and context curve over one shared window with one session-wide scale, so scrub-live's chosen time now has a concrete thing to line up with: a criterion says the chosen time is drawn against that same window, so its position agrees with the marks and the curve at that instant. Second, lane-activity confirmed the /agents payload is refetched as ingest coalesces and the window's end moves, so scrub-live's live-mode criterion now says live mode keeps following as later data extends the window. Third, lane-activity hit content records that report a body_length but carry no body and no body_ref - which is why the collector needed a length-preferring helper - so context-at-time gains a criterion that such a block is shown as its reported size with the text stated to be absent, instead of an empty context. context-at-time also gains a criterion binding its tool listing to the same lane and the same time bound as the context, which is cheap now because lane-activity already serves each lane's tool and API calls with times and names on the /agents payload; that same fact re-confirms keeping the merged tools-at-time inside it rather than re-splitting. The provability criterion stays on both open increments: it is the difference between timeline-landing's two correction rounds and lane-activity's zero. Order unchanged: scrub-live before context-at-time, because context-at-time answers for exactly the chosen time scrub-live establishes.
